component_records.title: Program governance, compliance and contract management
component_records.description: A Compliance and Contracts Lead owns every legal, administrative and reporting obligation from proposal through close-out: restricted-period contact discipline through the designated ESD contacts only, no gifts or employment discussions with ESD personnel, conflict-of-interest and prior non-responsibility disclosures, and ongoing 139-j/139-k form updates. The same lead runs the procurement calendar: all questions are submitted in writing by email to AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov before the August 29, 2025 deadline, with ESD's September 12, 2025 answers reviewed and reflected in the final submission, and no oral questions raised. The component maintains the Vendor Responsibility registration and questionnaire currency, professional-standards and no-charge rework commitments, the 30-day change-order claim window with continued performance, staff approval and substitution procedures, and the no-assignment/no-unapproved-subcontracting rules. It also holds the insurance program (CGL $1M/$2M, auto $1M where a vehicle is used, Sexual Abuse and Molestation $1M, statutory WC/Disability/Employer's Liability, ESD as additional insured, waiver of subrogation), accepts Schedule A, and manages OSC approval as a gating milestone before work starts. Proposal preparation costs are borne by us and the response-information waiver is accepted on submission.

component_records.title: MWBE, SDVOB and workforce diversity compliance
component_records.description: A dedicated Supplier Diversity Manager builds and executes the 30% MWBE and 6% SDVOB participation plans, submitting the MWBE and SDVOB Utilization Plans (Form OCSD-4) with the proposal and reporting compliance quarterly and monthly thereafter. The component documents good faith efforts in the form ESD requires — solicitations issued to certified firms, responses received, reasons for non-selection, meetings attended and scope-structuring steps — files evidence through the New York State Contract System, and manages notices of deficiency within seven business days and any waiver requests on Form OCSD-5. It also delivers the quarterly Workforce Utilization Report including gross wages per Executive Order #162, the monthly SDVOB compliance report by the 10th of each month to OCSD@esd.ny.gov, and revised utilization plans for any post-award changes. Human Rights Law certification, non-discrimination commitments including prior-conviction protections, and the NYS-business encouragement form are handled here.

component_records.title: Mobilization, curriculum development and industry partnership
component_records.description: In the first two months we finalize an industry-informed AI curriculum for both tracks, built with input from leading researchers and industry experts and reviewed by an employer advisory council that also commits to internships and hires. Track A content is sequenced around academic-year and summer delivery to align with employer internship hiring cycles; Track B is an accelerated, immersive bootcamp-style alternative to a degree, offered part-time or full-time. The curriculum includes real-world machine learning projects, mentorship, professional development, and stated credentials on completion, with a defined refresh cycle tied to employer demand. Employer partner letters committing to paid internships and full-time roles are secured and maintained, and the curriculum is mapped to the skill-attainment metrics used later for evaluation.

component_records.title: Outreach, recruitment, application and needs assessment
component_records.description: A targeted outreach and recruitment engine reaches low-income matriculating undergraduates for Track A and unemployed, underemployed and underrepresented New Yorkers with barriers to employment for Track B, working through colleges, community organizations and nonprofit partners. A single application and evaluation process screens for eligibility and readiness, applies a published low-income definition, and routes accepted participants into a documented needs assessment that identifies barriers (transportation, childcare, device and connectivity access, time) and assigns the supports to address them. The component tracks applicant, enrollment and completion counts with low-income percentages from day one, and is designed to enroll at least 250 participants with more than 50% low-income, targeting above 400 to earn ESD's priority consideration.

component_records.title: Training delivery, stipends and wrap-around supports
component_records.description: Both tracks are delivered as online AI courses with live instruction, mentorship and real-world machine learning projects, with Track A running alongside the academic year or summer and Track B running as a part-time or full-time immersive cohort. Every participant receives a stipend and wrap-around supports: an assigned mentor with industry expertise, a success coach, and career coaching throughout training. Skill-attainment is measured at defined checkpoints against the curriculum's competency map, and professional development — interview practice, portfolio and networking — runs through the program. Stipend levels and the training-versus-stipend cost split are set in the budget within the $2M per track cap, with no indirect costs included.

component_records.title: Internship and job placement pipeline
component_records.description: A placement team works each participant against a defined pathway: Track A participants are matched to paid internships with leading New York technology companies, with coaching to convert internships into full-time offers; Track B participants receive full-time AI job connection support from mid-cohort onward. The team maintains an employer pipeline with committed openings, runs mock interviews and employer showcases, and tracks paid internship placement rate and full-time job placement rate with low-income breakdowns. Placement targets are set so the majority of graduates secure paid internships or full-time AI or closely related employment, and the pipeline is designed to build a durable talent channel for AI employers in New York.

component_records.title: Data, performance measurement and ESD reporting
component_records.description: A data and reporting analyst operates a participant data system that captures, at minimum, applicant counts and low-income percentages, enrollment and completion counts with low-income percentages, paid internship placement rate and low-income share, full-time placement rate and low-income share, participating colleges and universities, and participating employer partners. The same system produces the skill-attainment metrics, the annual performance estimates against ESD's three headline metrics, and the quarterly and monthly compliance reports, and makes data available to ESD on request in ESD's format. Reporting scope is confirmed at contract negotiation and the system is built to absorb additional fields without re-platforming.

component_records.title: Budget, pricing and cost justification
component_records.description: A line-by-line price proposal is built for each track within the $2M cap, with Personnel Services broken out by job title, named employee where known, hourly or annual rate, fringe rate, percent of time and cost to contract, and Other Than Personnel Services on separate lines with quantities and cost to contract. The budget maps to Staff Salary and Benefits, Wraparound Supports and Participant Stipend Level, and other program costs such as curriculum development, marketing and events, excludes all indirect costs, and is mapped to the 18-month program duration. Any cost match is stated in ESD's budget template to earn the additional scoring credit, and every line carries a written justification.

component_records.title: Program management, staffing and dual-track capacity
component_records.description: A Program Management Office led by a Program Director runs both tracks under one governance model, with separate Track Leads, shared recruitment and data functions, and a single escalation path to ESD. Key personnel are named with one-page resumes, staff are subject to ESD approval, and any proposed change is notified immediately with a substitute summary and interview opportunity; we commit to keeping assigned staff through completion. items.text: ESD's Office of Strategic Workforce Development (OSWD) was created under Governor Hochul's April 2022 $350 million workforce development investment and is charged with aligning workforce efforts with employer needs and creating opportunities for unemployed, underemployed and underrepresented workers in the state's highest-growth sectors.
